commits.pr_title: [Docker] Compile Python bytecode at image build time
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fresh containers compile thousands of Python files during startup. This PR sets `UV_COMPILE_BYTECODE=1` in eight Dockerfiles, moving that work into image construction through uv's existing option.

## Current CI (September 24)

[CI 91034](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/91034) is running on `da0a5f6ed074`. The [H100 fault-tolerance job](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/91034#01a0d50c-2031-49c0-ba53-07b204574241) now passes both tests with #58593 included. The nightly dependency check also [passed its one retry](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/91034#01a0d546-42ce-499d-8f60-5ba7cfd9fac9), after SQLAlchemy's compatible wheel became available.

The [structured-output failure](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/91034#01a0d50c-202c-4b63-9825-46865a4c852a) repeats with the same parameter and output on main [91027](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/91027) and [91036](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/91036). B200 Mooncake already has an [automatic retry](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/91034#01a0d550-1a3d-44f0-b04a-721008e9d67b) queued. [AMD 13576](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/13576) timed out after slow checkpoint loading; its later stall remains unexplained. That native job consumes a wheel built before the changed final-image stage. Other jobs are still running.

The diff remains eight ENV lines plus one blank line. Pre-commit and paired Linux CPU Dockerfile definition checks pass, with the same two existing warnings as main. The head is unchanged while this run finishes.

## Results

### Matched build, delivery, and serving

I built `470fe3942ecdb889b2f3c0b57ace4b09d61dd103` with and without the CUDA Dockerfile ENV line (`vllm-openai`, CUDA sm_89, Python 3.12.3, Torch 2.13.0+cu130, uv 0.12.10). Source, interpreter, 244 Python distributions, 26,734 Python files, native payloads, and non-bytecode site-packages bytes matched. Each observation pulled from a loopback registry into an empty Docker store, then served local/offline Qwen3-0.6B through the first correct HTTP completion on one RTX 4090 Laptop with a four-CPU quota.

| Artifact | Compressed runtime layers | Median pull to correct response |
|---|---:|---:|
| Control, gzip | 8,511,741,380 bytes | 155.7265 s |
| Bytecode, gzip | 8,664,824,384 bytes | 144.5137 s |

The bytecode image adds 153,083,004 compressed bytes (+1.7985%). Its median paired saving is **15.3606 s**, n=3 pairs, and all three pairs improved. Five independent next-token checks and four-request bursts passed per activation with matching choices and usage. Candidate import compiled zero source files; control import compiled 5,257. Bypassing candidate caches restored 5,478 compilations.

### Native serving attribution

In a separate installed vLLM 0.28.0 experiment, the same 8.85 GB of Python and shared-object files were 100% page-resident before every start. First-correct-response medians were **57.0394 s without bytecode and 47.6911 s with it**, with a **10.1300 s median paired saving**, n=3 pairs; all pairs and output checks passed. The measured startup saving includes avoided compilation, cache-file work, and normal parent/child reuse. It is not entirely compiler CPU. [Protocol, observations, and limits](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55422#issuecomment-5608794542).

### Direct compiler reproduction

The exact 5,118-file import corpus, 78.60 MB and about 2.16 million source lines, was read into memory and compiled without execution or bytecode writes. Native CPython 3.12.3 took **6.3033 s median**, n=3 whole-corpus passes. A real uncached serving-CLI import took 12.2019 s with 6.9880 s inside 5,118 compiler calls; cached import took 5.0095 s and made zero compiler calls. Source hashes and 196 package versions match the resident-page study, but the Python binary build changed, so absolute times are not interchangeable. To reproduce without vLLM or a GPU, invoke `compile(source_bytes, filename, "exec", dont_inherit=True, optimize=0)` over the recorded trace paths in a fresh `python3.12 -I -S -B` process after preloading the sources.

### Inclusive import roots

Fresh-process medians below use fully resident source/native pages, n=3 paired runs per root. Rows include transitive imports and are **not additive**. Paired-saving medians need not equal differences of arm medians.

| Entry point | No bytecode | Bytecode | Median paired saving |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `import torch` | 2.1306 s | 0.8025 s | 1.3281 s |
| `import transformers` | 1.2943 s | 0.6760 s | 0.6018 s |
| `import vllm` | 6.7075 s | 2.1068 s | 4.6007 s |
| `import vllm.entrypoints.cli.serve` | 12.2659 s | 5.0198 s | 7.2461 s |

In this vLLM 0.28.0 environment (Torch 2.13.0, Transformers 5.17.0), bare Torch did not load Dynamo, Inductor, or SymPy; importing vLLM loaded all three. Bare Transformers did not load Torch. One eager path is the Inductor patch in `vllm.env_override`. Dependency-file ownership therefore does not tell us which entry point introduces the import cost.

### Bytecode portability

Pure-Python timestamp and checked-hash caches created on macOS ARM64, CPython 3.12.13 loaded unchanged on Linux x86-64, CPython 3.12.3 with source compilation blocked. Both used cache tag `cpython-312` and magic `cb0d0d0a`; all nine reuse and validation cases matched their expected outcomes. [Python documents compiled modules as architecture-independent](https://docs.python.org/3.12/tutorial/modules.html#compiled-python-files), with compatible interpreter format still required. The image pins its Python/native platform; the PR compiles within that build path and retains source. This fixture is not a full cross-platform vLLM deployment.

### Known caveats

uv [recommends bytecode compilation for production images](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/guides/integration/docker/#compiling-bytecode), trading build work and image size for startup time. The upstream issues I found concern [reproducible cache/image bytes](https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/129724) and [compilation hangs under affected QEMU-user setups](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/issues/6105). I reproduced the former on Mac CPython 3.12.13: identical source and checked-hash headers produced different serialized bytes depending on compilation order, but equal decoded code objects and correct execution. We should not claim reproducible image digests. The QEMU report concerns the build environment; native CUDA validation does not qualify emulated builds. No cache-format or concurrency workaround is added by this PR.

<details>
<summary>Secondary observations, reproduction details, and limits</summary>

Native serving pairs, without/with bytecode: 54.7488/44.6188 s, 57.0394/47.6911 s, and 60.6387/48.4054 s. Its separate September 9 CLI trace measured 8.1962 s in 5,118 source-compilation calls. The September 15 preloaded direct-compile passes were 6.2461, 6.3033 and 6.3194 s; their Python 3.12.3 build is newer, despite matching source hashes and package versions.

Separate diagnostic import-root traces measured compiler time/source files as Torch 1.3441 s/871, Transformers 0.6780 s/398, vLLM 4.7605 s/2,293 and serving CLI 7.5139 s/5,118. These hooked traces are excluded from the uninstrumented root medians above. The cached serving trace made zero compiler calls. Within the uncached CLI trace, exclusive compiler costs by source-file owner were Torch 2.852 s, SymPy 1.032 s, Transformers 0.498 s and vLLM 0.431 s, plus other dependencies. These are compiler timings, not inclusive package-import durations.

The earlier unchanged-runtime mechanism fixture used the published vLLM 0.28.0 image plus `python3 -m compileall -q -j 8 /usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages`. With image and model present, medians were 63.967 s control and 51.953 s bytecode, with a 12.014 s median paired saving, n=5. With the image absent and model present, loopback pull-through-response medians were 145.041 s and 134.109 s, with a 10.337 s median paired saving, n=3. Its added gzip layer was 153,159,438 bytes. This fixture isolates the mechanism but is not a matched full build of this PR.

Exact-head paired pull-through-response observations were 149.8156/134.4550 s, 155.7265/144.5137 s, and 162.3850/146.2806 s for control/bytecode. Host source pages were warm or uncontrolled in that experiment. The same bytecode artifact exported with the separate opt-in zstd change was 17.7633% smaller than control and saved 37.7032 s median paired, but those combined numbers include both changes and are not this PR's isolated effect.

The full-build recipes shared one recorded host-network preparation because the rig lacks `docker0`. The first control build failed in 1.32 s before installation; no timed cell was affected. Build durations, 688.83 s control and 629.16 s candidate, are not a matched build-time comparison. In the older delivery fixture, one post-timing mount cleanup failed after the clock and functional checks; that observation was retained without replacement and cleanup was resolved before continuing. The resident-page study retained two excluded preparation attempts and corrected a TCP cleanup probe before its six measured cells. The import-root study's first preparation reached 98.0101% residency and timed no imports; equal mmap page touches then produced 100% residency without relaxing the gate.

These are one-host medians with local models, no Internet transfer, warm or controlled pages as stated, and no p95 or throughput claim. They do not validate missing-model startup, every accelerator image, published multi-platform size, slow links, fleets, pip installs, or the earlier A10/Qwen3-8B baseline. Normal source-backed loader validation has limits: a corrupt marshalled body can fail without source fallback, and timestamp caches can accept changed same-size/same-mtime source. uv initially compiled only the reinstalled vLLM distribution in the package study, so the ENV line alone does not prove complete cache coverage for every image variant.

</details>

Related to #48193. An open-PR title search for bytecode on September 15 returned only this PR. AI assistance was used for implementation, experiment tooling, and analysis.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][PP] Skip sampled-token broadcasts whose requests leave the engine
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Under pipeline parallelism, `PPHandler.receive`/`broadcast`/`broadcast_drafts` only skip the sampled-token collective for **non-final** prefill chunks (`compute_need_sampled_mask`). Every other sample-producing batch runs the broadcast — including final prefill chunks whose request leaves the engine right after the sample:

- Disaggregated prefill submits `max_tokens=1`, so the final chunk's single token is handed off to the decode instance and the request finishes (`FINISHED_LENGTH`) on this engine.
- The deferred consumer (`get_prev_sampled_outputs`) discards that payload via its freed-request filter anyway — non-last ranks only use the broadcast tokens to build the inputs of a follow-up step for the same request, and there is none.
- The collective still couples all PP ranks at every request boundary and contends with the next chunk's activation p2p transfer. With short prompts (e.g. 8k / 4096-token chunks = 2 chunks per request) this drain dominates and shows up as per-chunk stalls between PP stages during chunked prefill.

This PR gathers `RequestState.max_seq_len` (`prompt_len + max_tokens`) into the per-step `InputBatch` (via `BatchReqState`, alongside `prefill_len_np`) and extends `compute_need_sampled_mask` to also exclude final prefill chunks whose single sampled token reaches the request's length cap (`prefill_len + 1 >= max_seq_len`). When every sample-producing row is such a request, the mask returns `None` and all three entry points take their existing no-op path — no collective is posted on either side. Both PP ranks derive the verdict from identical per-step batch/request state, so sender and receivers always agree.

The condition is per-request and role-agnostic: it fires for `max_tokens=1` requests on dedicated prefill instances and on hybrid producer-consumer deployments alike, while any batch where a request keeps decoding on this engine retains the broadcast.

Safety property preserved: **decoding rows are never excluded.** Speculative decoding advances `num_computed_tokens` several tokens per step and can transiently overrun `prompt_len + max_tokens` while the scheduler still runs the request; predicting "this one is finishing" would freeze the earlier stages' `last_sampled_tokens`/`draft_tokens` and desynchronize the PP stages (this hazard is exactly what `test_keeps_decoding_request_past_its_length_cap` documents — that test is unchanged and still passes).

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/v1/worker/test_pp_utils.py` — extended with:
  - `test_excludes_final_prefill_chunk_reaching_its_length_cap` (max_tokens=1 final chunk → mask `None`)
  - `test_keeps_final_prefill_chunk_with_generation_budget_left`
  - `test_length_cap_overrun_decode_row_is_kept` (decode row past its cap still broadcast)
  - `test_finishing_prefill_row_does_not_drop_a_sibling_row` (mixed batch keeps the sibling row)
  - the four pre-existing mask tests are unchanged and pass (behavior identical when `max_seq_len_np` is `None`, e.g. dummy/capture batches).
- ruff check / ruff format / mypy clean on the changed files.

## Test Result

- All `compute_need_sampled_mask` cases (4 pre-existing + 4 new) validated locally; pre-commit ruff/format/mypy/SPDX hooks pass (two unrelated hooks fail only under the local Python 3.9 toolchain — `itertools.pairwise` / `X | None` at runtime — and pass under the repo's pinned Python).
- NPU/GPU end-to-end effect (PP2×TP8 disaggregated prefill, chunked prefill request-boundary stalls removed) verified on the vLLM-Ascend deployment where this was profiled; the equivalent plugin-side change is tracked in vllm-project/vllm-ascend#17500.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Don't let a structured-output request sample from an unmasked row
commits.pr_body:
> This pull request was developed and reviewed with support from the Linux Club of Peking University (LCPU). For questions, please contact linuxclub@pku.edu.cn. ## Purpose Part of #54437. `StructuredOutputManager.grammar_bitmask` constrains a row only while `apply_bitmask` holds, and a `-1` placeholder in the scheduled draft window sets `seen_padding`, so every row after it is filled with `_full_mask` — every token in the vocabulary allowed: ```python # vllm/v1/structured_output/__init__.py for i, token in enumerate(req_tokens): apply_bitmask = not failed and not seen_padding and i >= constraint_start self._fill_bitmasks(((grammar, cumulative_index, apply_bitmask),)) if token == -1: seen_padding = True ``` That is sound when the `-1` means "`validate_tokens` rejected this draft": the first `-1` then sits at exactly the draft the grammar rejected, that draft's own row is still masked, so it is rejected and acceptance never reaches the permissive rows. It is not sound when the `-1` means "the drafts never reached the scheduler", which happens because the draft hand-off carries no identity — `DraftTokensHandler` keeps one slot that every `execute_model` overwrites (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/utils.py`), and it also clears the payload entirely for a batch with no structured-output requests. The worker meanwhile verifies the genuine drafts from its own GPU-resident `req_states.draft_tokens`, so acceptance can walk straight into rows that constrain nothing and the request emits tokens the grammar never allowed. #54437 has the full chain, a model-free reproduction on `main`, and field measurements. This PR is the fail-closed half: it makes the permissive rows unreachable regardless of why the drafts went missing. The identity fix for the hand-off is a separate change. **Not a duplicate of #56802.** That PR implements the other half of #54437 — identity for the hand-off, so the drafts are not lost in the first place. It is complementary: its lookup miss path falls back to exactly the invalidation this PR adds, so on a miss without this PR the bitmask still fails open. ## Change Carry, per structured-output request, how many leading drafts the bitmask actually constrained, and invalidate the drafts from that index on, so `is_valid_draft = draft_sampled >= 0` pins the accepted length before sampling can reach a permissive row. - `vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py`: `get_grammar_bitmask` fills `num_acceptable_drafts` with `len(strip_speculative_padding(window))`, reusing the helper #48200 introduced. - `vllm/v1/core/sched/output.py`: `GrammarOutput.num_acceptable_drafts`, a defaulted field, so existing constructors keep working. - `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/structured_outputs.py`: `grammar_invalid_drafts` turns that into a mask over logit rows, built on device: a draft is invalid when its local position exceeds its request's `num_acceptable_drafts`. The local position is `expanded_local_pos`, which `expand_idx_mapping` derives from the device `cu_num_logits` — the same (request, position) keying `apply_grammar_bitmask` uses, so it stays correct when adaptive verification trims drafts on device and `cu_num_logits_np` is only an upper bound. When every request's scheduled drafts are within its limit (fully back-filled, the normal case) it returns `None` on the CPU and launches nothing. - `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py`: `sample()` calls it after applying the bitmask and hands the mask to the rejection sampler. - `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/rejection_sampler.py`: verification runs against `draft_sampled.masked_fill(mask, -1)`. `apply_sampling_params` and the watermarking context still receive the real draft ids, so penalties and bad-words are unaffected. - `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/batch_shard.py`: shard the new per-request list the same way as the bitmask. No kernel change: `rejection_sampler_utils` already resamples a `-1` position straight from the target distribution rather than from the residual. That matters — `max(p - q, 0)` is the residual of a *genuine* rejection, and forcing one where `p ≈ q` collapses it across the vocabulary. When the drafts are fully back-filled nothing is invalidated and behaviour is unchanged. Absent the field — an older scheduler, or warmup — the whole window is invalidated, which is the conservative choice. Production diff is 85 added / 3 removed lines across those six files. ## Test Plan ```bash # Unit coverage for the new helper, plus the suites this PR's call paths touch. .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/worker/test_grammar_invalid_drafts.py \ tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_rejection_sampler_chunking.py \ tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_batch_shard.py \ tests/v1/structured_output/test_structured_output_manager.py -q ``` `tests/v1/worker/test_grammar_invalid_drafts.py` — 5 cases covering `grammar_invalid_drafts`: whole window, partial window, nothing to do, per-request offset, and **adaptive verification with an uneven reallocation** (the device layout differs from `cu_num_logits_np`). **End-to-end reproduction.** Not committed, per review. Save the file below as `tests/v1/worker/test_grammar_fail_closed.py` and run it on `main` and on this branch: ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/worker/test_grammar_fail_closed.py -q ``` It drives the real `GPUModelRunner.sample()` → `apply_grammar_bitmask` → `RejectionSampler` path with a bitmask whose leading rows carry a real mask and whose later rows are `_full_mask`, and with the drafts the worker holds on the GPU disagreeing with the scheduler's padded copy, which is what a lost hand-off produces. Temperature 0, one request, four logit rows, so it is deterministic.
tests/v1/worker/test_grammar_fail_closed.py ```python # SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0 # SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project """Acceptance must stop at the last bitmask row that carries a real mask. `grammar_bitmask` stops constraining rows once it meets a -1 placeholder in the scheduled draft window, and the worker verifies the drafts it holds on the GPU rather than the scheduler's padded copy. When the two disagree -- the hand-off lost a step's drafts, see #54437 -- acceptance can walk into a row where every token is allowed. The grammar here admits only LEGAL. The scheduled window is back-filled one draft deep, so rows 0 and 1 carry a real mask and rows 2.. are `_full_mask`, while the drafts on the GPU would carry acceptance into row 2 and emit ILLEGAL. """ from types import SimpleNamespace import numpy as np import pytest import torch from vllm.platforms import current_platform from vllm.utils.math_utils import cdiv from vllm.v1.core.sched.output import GrammarOutput from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.model_runner import GPUModelRunner from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.sample.states import NO_LOGPROBS from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.rejection_sampler import RejectionSampler from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.structured_outputs import StructuredOutputsWorker VOCAB = 128 K = 3 # drafts per step NUM_LOGITS = K + 1 # + the bonus row LEGAL = 7 ILLEGAL = 99 # Index of the first -1 in the scheduled window: rows 0..1 are masked. NUM_ACCEPTABLE = 1 def _bitmask() -> np.ndarray: """Rows 0..NUM_ACCEPTABLE constrained to LEGAL, the rest fully permissive.""" mask = np.zeros((NUM_LOGITS, cdiv(VOCAB, 32)), dtype=np.int32) for row in range(NUM_LOGITS): if row <= NUM_ACCEPTABLE: mask[row, LEGAL // 32] = 1 << (LEGAL % 32) else: mask[row, :] = -1 # every token allowed return mask def _input_batch(device: torch.device) -> SimpleNamespace: cu_np = np.array([0, NUM_LOGITS], dtype=np.int32) # draft_sampled = input_ids[logits_indices]; entry i + 1 is draft i, so the # drafts the GPU holds are [LEGAL, LEGAL, ILLEGAL]. input_ids = torch.tensor( [LEGAL, LEGAL, LEGAL, ILLEGAL], dtype=torch.int32, device=device ) return SimpleNamespace( num_reqs=1, req_ids=["g"], num_draft_tokens=K, num_draft_tokens_per_req=np.array([K], dtype=np.int32), input_ids=input_ids, logits_indices=torch.arange(NUM_LOGITS, dtype=torch.int32, device=device), positions=torch.arange(NUM_LOGITS, dtype=torch.int64, device=device), cu_num_logits_np=cu_np, cu_num_logits=torch.from_numpy(cu_np).to(device), idx_mapping_np=np.array([0], dtype=np.int32), idx_mapping=torch.zeros(1, dtype=torch.int32, device=device), expanded_idx_mapping=torch.zeros(NUM_LOGITS, dtype=torch.int32, device=device), expanded_local_pos=torch.arange(NUM_LOGITS, dtype=torch.int32, device=device), seq_lens=torch.tensor([64], dtype=torch.int32, device=device), seq_lens_cpu_upper_bound=torch.tensor([64], dtype=torch.int32), ) def _logits(device: torch.device) -> torch.Tensor: """Every row prefers its own draft, so nothing but the mask can reject one.""" logits = torch.zeros(NUM_LOGITS, VOCAB, dtype=torch.float32, device=device) logits[0, LEGAL] = 10.0 logits[1, LEGAL] = 10.0 logits[2, ILLEGAL] = 10.0 # row 2 is permissive, so this wins there logits[3, LEGAL] = 10.0 return logits def _rejection_sampler(device: torch.device) -> RejectionSampler: sampler = object.__new__(RejectionSampler) sampler.num_speculative_steps = K sampler.enable_adaptive_verification = False sampler.use_block_verification = False sampler.synthetic_conditional_rates = None sampler.watermark_key = None zeros_f = torch.zeros(1, dtype=torch.float32, device=device) # greedy sampler.sampler = SimpleNamespace( compute_nans=False, logprobs_mode="raw_logprobs", use_fp64_gumbel=False, apply_sampling_params=lambda logits, *args, **kwargs: logits, sampling_states=SimpleNamespace( temperature=SimpleNamespace(gpu=zeros_f), seeds=SimpleNamespace(gpu=torch.zeros(1, dtype=torch.int64, device=device)), max_num_logprobs=lambda _: NO_LOGPROBS, ), req_states=SimpleNamespace( prefill_len=SimpleNamespace( gpu=torch.zeros(1, dtype=torch.int32, device=device) ) ), ) return sampler @pytest.mark.skipif(not current_platform.is_cuda(), reason="Requires CUDA") def test_acceptance_stops_at_the_last_masked_row(): device = torch.device("cuda") input_batch = _input_batch(device) logits = _logits(device) runner = object.__new__(GPUModelRunner) runner.device = device runner.vocab_size = VOCAB runner.batch_sharder = None runner.sampler = None runner.model = SimpleNamespace(compute_logits=lambda hidden: logits) runner.rejection_sampler = _rejection_sampler(device) runner.speculator = SimpleNamespace(draft_logits=None) runner.structured_outputs_worker = StructuredOutputsWorker( max_num_logits=NUM_LOGITS, vocab_size=VOCAB, device=device, mask_stride=NUM_LOGITS, num_bonus_tokens=1, ) grammar_output = GrammarOutput(["g"], _bitmask()) # The scheduler reports how many leading drafts the bitmask constrained. # Absent on an older scheduler, where the whole window is invalidated. grammar_output.num_acceptable_drafts = [NUM_ACCEPTABLE] hidden = torch.zeros(NUM_LOGITS, 8, dtype=torch.float32, device=device) sampler_output, num_sampled, _ = runner.sample(hidden, input_batch, grammar_output) accepted = int(num_sampled[0].item()) emitted = sampler_output.sampled_token_ids[0, :accepted].tolist() assert ILLEGAL not in emitted, ( f"emitted {emitted}: a draft verified against a permissive row was " f"accepted, so the request sampled with no grammar constraint" ) # Draft 0 may be accepted; draft 1 must not be, because accepting it moves # sampling into row 2, which constrains nothing. assert accepted == NUM_ACCEPTABLE + 1 assert emitted == [LEGAL] * accepted ```
## Test Result End-to-end reproduction on `main` @ `2798f668`: ``` E AssertionError: emitted [7, 7, 99, 7]: a draft verified against a permissive row was accepted, so the request sampled with no grammar constraint E assert 99 not in [7, 7, 99, 7] 1 failed, 14 warnings in 1.00s ``` Token 7 is the only token the grammar admits; token 99 is one it never admits. On this branch, same base: ``` 1 passed, 14 warnings in 1.26s ``` and the Test Plan selection is `71 passed, 1 xfailed`. ### Model evaluation One RTX 4090, `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`, Qwen3-8B + `Qwen3-8B-speculator.eagle3` (K=4), `--async-scheduling`, xgrammar. `lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --limit 200`: | | exact_match, strict-match | exact_match, flexible-extract | |---|---|---| | `main` @ `0bfc7a15` | 0.925 ± 0.0187 | 0.925 ± 0.0187 | | this PR @ `ec112592`, same base | 0.925 ± 0.0187 | 0.925 ± 0.0187 | gsm8k carries no structured-output requests, so that is the "speculative decoding is untouched" half. For the structured-output half, a mixed grammar + plain load with every grammar response validated against its JSON schema (4 concurrency mixes, 49 grammar requests) gives 0 schema violations, 0 `grammar rejected tokens` and 0 `Failed to advance FSM` on both `main` and this PR — which is the expected result at `pipeline_parallel_size=1`, where the hand-off does not get clobbered. Both were measured at `ec112592`. The review round since changed only how the invalid drafts are located, and that code runs only for a batch that holds a structured-output request whose drafts were not fully back-filled — which neither gsm8k (no grammar requests) nor the `pp=1` load (always fully back-filled) produces. I have not re-run them for that reason; happy to if you want the numbers on the current head. Beyond that: both this change and the identity fix have been running in production on a 2-node x 2-GPU deployment (`pipeline_parallel_size=2`, `tensor_parallel_size=2`, DeepSeek-V4-Flash with `dspark` speculative decoding, K=7, xgrammar). Before them, `tool_choice=required` and `json_schema` failed 100% of the time whenever a second structured-output request was resident; after, 72/72 concurrent grammar requests complete with zero `grammar rejected` lines and zero engine errors. Independently, @xinli-sw [reports](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54442#issuecomment-5822629259) that this PR fixes a `pipeline_parallel_size=2` x `tensor_parallel_size=8` deployment with DSpark (K=3) on 16x B200. ## AI assistance This PR contains AI-generated code. The root-cause analysis, the instrumentation behind the numbers in #54437, and the patch were produced with Claude, with the consumption-time-snapshot idea and the fail-closed requirement contributed by GPT-5.6. The adaptive-verification issue in review was caught by an AI reviewer and fixed with Claude. commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Stop vllm-bench chat latency at the last token
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Port #55508 to the Rust `vllm-bench` `openai-chat` backend.

#55508 fixed Python `vllm bench serve` so that the trailing choice-less `usage` chunk no longer advances the end of a request. The Rust port still updates `most_recent_timestamp` for every non-`[DONE]` message, and its comment still describes the old Python behavior. As a result, `latency` (E2EL) runs past the final token, `latency - ttft != sum(itl)`, and TPOT is inflated relative to ITL. This also means the Rust and Python clients disagree on the same server.

This PR moves `most_recent_timestamp = timestamp` inside the token branch, matching Python and the Rust `openai` (completions) backend, which already stops at the last token.

Found while investigating #59154. This PR does **not** explain the 3-4x gap reported there; that gap comes from temperature defaults, as analyzed in the issue thread.

## Not a duplicate

#55508 changed only the Python clients (`vllm/benchmarks/lib/endpoint_request_func.py`, `benchmarks/backend_request_func.py`); the Rust `vllm-bench` was not touched. I checked for open PRs covering the Rust side:

```bash
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "55508 in:body"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "vllm-bench latency"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "Rust bench usage chunk"
```

None of them touch `rust/src/bench/src/backends/openai_chat.rs`. The temperature-warning PR from #59154 (#59247) only touches `rust/src/bench/src/config.rs`, so there is no overlap.

## Test Plan

- New unit test `test_usage_chunk_does_not_extend_latency`. It starts a local raw-socket SSE server that sends 3 token chunks, waits 150 ms, then sends the usage chunk. The test asserts `latency - ttft == sum(itl)` and that `latency` excludes the 150 ms gap.
- `cargo test -p vllm-bench --lib`
- `cargo clippy -p vllm-bench --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- End-to-end: mock OpenAI server (TTFT 200 ms, 20 ms/token, 100 ms delay before the usage chunk), 128 prompts, `--max-concurrency 32`, `--random-input-len 128 --random-output-len 128`, before vs. after.

## Test Result

Unit test before the fix:
```
latency - ttft (0.15033325s) != sum(itl) (0.000682083s)
```
After the fix: `167 passed; 0 failed; 12 ignored`. Clippy and fmt are clean.

End-to-end against the mock server:

| | Mean TPOT (ms) | Mean ITL (ms) | Mean E2EL (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|
| before | 23.00 | 22.18 | 3131.35 |
| after | 22.18 | 22.18 | 3022.48 |

After the fix, TPOT equals ITL, and E2EL no longer includes the ~100 ms usage-chunk gap.

---

**AI assistance disclosure:** I used Claude (Claude Code) to help investigate and write this change. I reviewed every changed line, ran all the tests above locally, and reproduced the before/after numbers myself. The commit carries a `Co-Authored-By` trailer.

commits.pr_title: [Core] Include the LoRA path in prefix-cache block hashes
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Prefix-cache block hashes identify a LoRA adapter only by its name. If a name is
re-pointed at a different adapter (unload then load under the same name, or
`load_inplace` with a new path), requests for that name can reuse KV computed with the
previous adapter until those blocks are evicted. See #42125 and #30931.

This adds the adapter path to the LoRA extra key: `("lora", name, path)`.

- Re-pointing a name at an adapter stored elsewhere no longer reuses the old blocks.
- Hashes stay deterministic across instances: no file I/O, no per-process counter.
- Connectors and offload tiers keyed by block hash pick the change up automatically.
- KV events are unchanged: they publish only the LoRA name for this key.

An in-place reload from the same path with changed files still cannot be detected
without hashing the adapter's contents, so that case now logs a warning suggesting a new
path. Content-based versioning (as proposed in #48352) could be added on top of this key
later.

## Why this is not a duplicate

#48352 versions the LoRA key with a digest of the adapter's files. That handles
same-path content changes for local absolute paths, but it adds about 190 lines of file
hashing that runs on the API server's request path. This PR is the minimal,
deterministic fix for re-pointed names and is compatible with #48352 as a follow-up.

## Compatibility

Prefix-cache and external-store hashes change for LoRA blocks, so KV stored by an
earlier version for LoRA requests misses once after upgrade. Instances that serve the
same adapter from different absolute paths no longer share LoRA blocks with each other.

## Test Plan

```
pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
  tests/v1/core/prefix_cache tests/v1/simple_kv_offload \
  tests/distributed/test_kv_cache_events.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector tests/entrypoints/serve/lora \
  tests/entrypoints/serve/sagemaker/test_sagemaker_lora_adapters.py \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/completion/test_lora_resolvers.py
```

## Test Result

- New `test_lora_path_change_changes_block_hashes` fails without the change (2 failed)
  and passes with it.
- On 4x GB200, the command above gives 1013 passed, 8 skipped.
- The KV event tests are unchanged and pass, so the event format is unchanged.

## Purpose

## Purpose

This fixes two CI tests on main that fail for reasons unrelated to the code they test.

**1. `test_weight_sync_metrics_aggregate_across_api_servers`**, in (H200 MIG 35GB) and (MI355 DPX) Entrypoints Integration (API Server) 3. It failed on 5 main builds on 2026-09-30, the day #55781 added it: 92138, 92174, 92180, 92182 (MI355) and 92246. Each time it hit `assert 1 == 2` on `len(pids_that_recorded(tmp_path))`, while all the metric assertions passed.

The test assumed 25 connections would spread over both `--api-server-count 2` processes. The API servers accept from one shared listening socket, and SO_REUSEPORT only balances between separate sockets. So the kernel can give one process every connection.

The test now keeps syncing until both processes have recorded, with a minimum of 8 syncs and a cap of 64. It then checks the counts against the number of syncs actually sent.

**2. The Mooncake PD accuracy script** (`tests/v1/kv_connector/mooncake_integration/run_accuracy_test.sh`) used fixed ports: 8100+, 8200+, bootstrap 8998+, and proxy 8192. Its b200-k8s pods use host networking, so another job on the node can already hold those ports. Nightly 92059 failed with `[Errno 98] error while attempting to bind on address ('127.0.0.1', 8192): address already in use`. With host networking, a fixed port could also make `wait_for_server` see another job's server as ready.

The script now gets all its ports from the kernel in a single call that binds them at the same time, so they are distinct. It passes the proxy port to `test_accuracy.py` through `PROXY_PORT`, which defaults to 8192.

commits.pr_title: [CI] Deflake shutdown wait-timeout test by synchronizing on request admission
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

- Replace the fixed 0.5-second delay in
  `test_wait_timeout_completes_requests` with a bounded server-observed request
  admission barrier.
- Poll and parse the existing `vllm:num_requests_running` Prometheus gauge,
  summing all label sets before sending SIGTERM.
- Include the observed admission delay in the drain assertion so a future
  failure distinguishes admission failure from shutdown failure.

## Why

The test sends SIGTERM after sleeping for 0.5 seconds, then requires at least
one request to complete after the signal. The sleep does not guarantee that
EngineCore has admitted any work. If drain starts with an empty queue, that
postcondition cannot be satisfied.

`ShutdownState.inflight_requests` is not a valid substitute: it is incremented
before `client.completions.create(...)` is awaited, so it only establishes that
a client coroutine has started. The server's scheduler gauge directly observes
the state that the drain assertion depends on.

The race was first observed in Buildkite build 90220 on #52178 and was then
reproduced locally on unmodified upstream source. In the local reproduction,
EngineCore entered drain mode and immediately reported request processing
complete; the test ended with zero post-SIGTERM completions and ten connection
errors.

## Validation

Hardware and software:

- Ubuntu 22.04.5
- NVIDIA RTX 4090 24 GB, driver 580.105.08
- Python 3.12.3
- PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130 / CUDA 13.0

Baseline reproduction on unmodified source:

```text
test_wait_timeout_completes_requests: failed
requests_after_sigterm=0
connection_errors=10
got_500=True
```

A measurement-only run preserved the original 0.5-second delay and SIGTERM
timing and reported `ADMISSION_DELAY_SECONDS=None`. This is supporting evidence,
not an internal admission timestamp: scheduler-stat publication may lag. The
decisive evidence is the paired test failure and immediate empty drain.

Focused candidate results:

```bash
for i in $(seq 1 6); do
  VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=0 python -m pytest \
    tests/entrypoints/launchers/test_shutdown.py \
    -k test_wait_timeout_completes_requests -q || break
done
# 6/6 passed

for i in $(seq 1 6); do
  VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 python -m pytest \
    tests/entrypoints/launchers/test_shutdown.py \
    -k test_wait_timeout_completes_requests -q || break
done
# 6/6 passed
```

All twelve candidate runs reached `/metrics` and observed the running-request
gauge become positive before SIGTERM. A synthetic two-label metrics sample was
also parsed and summed correctly (`2 + 3 = 5.0`).

Static checks:

```text
pre-commit run ruff-check --files tests/entrypoints/launchers/test_shutdown.py: passed
pre-commit run ruff-format --files tests/entrypoints/launchers/test_shutdown.py: passed
pre-commit run typos --files tests/entrypoints/launchers/test_shutdown.py: passed
git diff --check: passed
```

The aggregate `pre-commit run --files` could not finish initializing an
unrelated actionlint Go environment because `proxy.golang.org` timed out; the
applicable hooks above completed successfully.

The validation used source at `2af05512c` with existing CUDA/Rust artifacts from
`6af44e288`, because the exact CUDA 13 nightly wheel was not yet published. The
test file, Python gauge logger, Rust gauge registration, and Rust `/metrics`
route are byte-identical between those commits. The candidate has since been
rebased onto current `main` at `91d7324c`; the target file did not change and
the rebased diff has the same stable patch ID as the validated diff.

Supplemental validation after the rebase used the exact PR head `e042c4f3` on
an NVIDIA RTX 4090 with Python 3.12.3, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, and CUDA 13.0:

```text
VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=0 ... test_shutdown.py -q
8 passed in 268.99s

VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 ... test_shutdown.py \
  -k "not engine_failure and not test_abort_timeout_exits_quickly" -q
7 passed, 1 deselected in 208.29s
```

The complete-file commands mirror the entrypoints job (Python frontend, whole
file) and the Rust-frontend coverage job's selector. Existing compatible native
artifacts were reused because this patch changes only the Python test.
The Rust selector deselects one test: `test_abort_timeout_exits_quickly` no
longer exists in this file, so only `engine_failure` matches.

## Duplicate-work check

Checked open PRs on 2026-09-22 using the exact test name and the terms
`shutdown timeout`, `admission`, and `num_requests_running`. No overlapping PR
was found. #56886 concerns a Rust gRPC discovery-withdrawal grace period and
does not modify this test or its admission precondition; #41834 is unrelated
kernel/model work.

## Scope

This is a test-only synchronization change. It does not modify serving behavior
or model output, so model evaluations are not applicable.

## AI assistance disclosure

AI assistance was used to investigate the failure, inspect the Python and Rust
metrics paths, prepare the patch, and review the validation evidence. The human
submitter reviewed the changed code and ran the reported tests.

commits.pr_title: [Docs] Add PR checklist skill for coding agents
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

(DISCLAIMER: I USED THE NEW SKILL TO HAVE GPT-6 AUTHOR THE PR DESCRIPTION BELOW, COMMIT THE CHANGES AND OPEN THIS PR. TREAT IT AS A REVIEWABLE EXAMPLE ARTIFACT. ALL CODE CHANGES WERE HAND WRITTEN WITH CARE BY ME.)

Add a `pr-checklist` skill for coding agents preparing, reviewing, or revising
vLLM pull requests. Integrate it with the agent contribution instructions and
the PR template.

## Claims

- Provide a structured review workflow covering design fit, compatibility,
  complexity, tradeoffs, validation, test quality, code clarity, and PR evidence.
- Distinguish validation performed for a contribution from tests maintained in
  the repository, emphasizing meaningful coverage rather than test volume.
- Include guidance for human-in-the-loop review and responding to prior feedback.
- Require agents to use the skill before submission through `AGENTS.md`.
- Restructure the PR template around Overview, Claims, Validation, and Details,
  with checklist and AI-assistance disclosure fields.

The intended benefit is better-prepared contributions and less avoidable
maintainer follow-up. This PR does not claim a measured reduction in review
rounds or review time.

## Validation

This change is documentation and agent instructions only. No serving-engine,
model, kernel, dependency, or runtime behavior is modified; runtime tests,
model evaluations, and performance benchmarks are not applicable.

### Diff and structure checks

```bash
git status --short
git diff -- AGENTS.md .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md
git ls-files --others --exclude-standard .agents/skills/pr-checklist
git diff --check
git diff --no-index --check /dev/null .agents/skills/pr-checklist/SKILL.md
wc -l AGENTS.md .agents/skills/pr-checklist/SKILL.md
```

- Reviewed the two tracked-file diffs and the complete new skill.
- Confirmed the proposed change consists of those three files; research data,
  scraping scripts, plots, and intermediate drafts are excluded.
- `AGENTS.md` has 159 lines and the skill has 153 lines, within the applicable
  instruction-document budgets.
- The tracked-file whitespace check produced no diagnostics.
- The new skill's whitespace check reports one trailing space on the helper
  inlining instruction. This remains in the proposed diff.
- No Markdown linter or documentation build was run.

### Current-skill behavioral smoke test

A fresh agent context read the current skill and applied it to four
hypothetical scenarios without executing tests or changing files:

1. **This documentation-only PR:** recognized runtime validation as not
   applicable and assessed workflow consistency and documentation.
2. **Reviewing another author's optimization PR:** requested missing
   configuration, correctness, and serving-performance evidence rather than
   skipping the PR-contents section.
3. **Re-review with an unresolved backend concern:** traced related paths,
   requested appropriate evidence, and identified a stale description.
4. **Intentional all-drafts-rejected regression test:** identified a conflict
   between the expected zero acceptance and the skill's nonzero-acceptance
   instruction. This remains an outstanding caveat below.

These are qualitative instruction-following checks, not automated regression
tests or evidence of real-world review-time savings.

## Details

### Motivation and research

The drafting process examined the latest 50 vLLM PRs reviewed by each of
`benchislett` and `mgoin`, ordered by the reviewer's latest submitted review.
The samples contain 97 distinct PRs and 342 nonempty authored review/comment
messages. Recurring themes included compatibility across execution paths,
appropriate ownership and reuse, concise implementations, meaningful rather
than excessive tests, and claims supported by evidence.

A separate exploratory analysis measured additions and deletions under
`vllm/` and compared them with description-based complexity grades. It
reinforced that LOC is a coarse review aid, not a reliable standalone semantic
complexity classification. The skill's 50/250 bands are judgment-based
guidance, not validated predictive cutoffs.

The research artifacts are local preparation material and are not included
in this PR. The proposed skill was handwritten and iteratively refined by
the human author with AI-assisted research and review.

### Duplicate-work checks

Open-PR searches were run on September 15, 2026:

```bash
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open \
  --search '"pr-checklist"' --limit 30 --json number,title,url,headRefName
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open \
  --search '"skill" "review"' --limit 30 --json number,title,url,headRefName
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open \
  --search 'checklist in:title' --limit 30 --json number,title,url
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open \
  --search 'skill in:title' --limit 30 --json number,title,url
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open \
  --head 'benchislett:skill-pr-checklist' --json number,title,url
```

The broad searches returned unrelated PRs mentioning review or checklist
usage. Targeted title searches found checklists for tool-calling models and
server hardening, and skills for CI and installation; none appeared to
duplicate this general contribution-review workflow. No existing open PR
was found for this branch. No associated issue was supplied, so issue-specific
duplicate checks were not applicable.

### AI assistance

AI assistance was used for GitHub review-history collection, qualitative
categorization, exploratory LOC analysis, draft review, behavioral smoke
checks, and preparation of this description. The human submitter remains
responsible for reviewing and understanding every changed line.

---

<details>
<summary>Pull Request Checklist</summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill.
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.
- [x] **Design Fit:** Adds a focused skill and integrates it into the contribution workflow without runtime changes.
- [ ] **Testing and Validation:** Documentation checks and behavioral smoke cases were run; the rejection-test instruction caveat and whitespace diagnostic remain outstanding.
- [ ] **Code Quality and Style:** Review the helper instruction and invocation/disclosure wording noted above; no lint pass has been claimed.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Describes the purpose, scope, evidence, duplicate-work checks, limitations, and AI assistance.

</details>

commits.pr_title: [Mamba] Add FlashInfer ReplaySSM support for MTP
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

This stacked follow-up extends the native FlashInfer ReplaySSM integration from single-token decode in #52506 to multi-token prediction (MTP) verification for Mamba2 models.

With MTP, the model evaluates one target token plus several draft tokens before sampling determines how many were accepted. ReplaySSM avoids materializing a separate recurrent state for every speculative token: each layer keeps a checkpoint and a ring of inputs, the accepted length advances a shared cursor before the next forward, and the checkpoint is updated only when the next verification window would overflow the ring.

## Dependencies

> [!IMPORTANT]
> This PR is stacked on #52506 and must not merge independently. Until #52506 lands, GitHub shows the cumulative base and MTP changes in this diff.

The FlashInfer path also depends on the compatible ReplaySSM API and native autotuning work in [flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4545](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4545).

## Design

- **MTP-shaped execution:** uniform verification batches use dense `(batch, tokens, ...)` inputs so FlashInfer can select its native MTP tactics. Variable-length batches use the packed `cu_seqlens` interface.
- **One acceptance update per cache group:** every Mamba layer observes the same accepted-token count, so ring cursors are shared and advanced once per model forward. Checkpoints and ring payloads remain layer-local.
- **One state page per request:** ReplaySSM stores one physical Mamba state page rather than one page per target/draft position. The causal-conv1d verification length is passed separately from the physical block-table width.
- **CUDA-graph-safe indexing:** the contiguous FlashInfer state-index vector lives in persistent runner-owned storage and is refreshed before replay, keeping its captured address stable.
- **Native FlashInfer selection:** the ReplaySSM call uses FlashInfer’s `checkpointing_ssu` API and native autotuning. PDL is forwarded explicitly but defaults off because it was not a consistent end-to-end win.
- **No duplicate Triton implementation:** #49847 implements MTP ReplaySSM using separate Triton kernels, a token-major ring, and its own cursor lifecycle. This PR retains the FlashInfer layout and delegates the update to native FlashInfer instead of copying the Triton kernel stack into vLLM.

This PR does not modify FlashInfer or add prefix-cache alignment support. ReplaySSM continues to use `mamba_cache_mode=none`.

## Correctness

Matched GSM8K evaluation on GB200 compared FlashInfer ReplaySSM with the exact #49847 Triton implementation:

| Backend | Correct | Accuracy | Invalid outputs |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| FlashInfer | 437 / 512 | 85.35% | 0 |
| Triton #49847 | 437 / 512 | 85.35% | 0 |

The comparison used FP32 SSM state with stochastic rounding disabled. A strict H100 B16/AL1 CUDA-graph control also produced identical complete output hashes across the two backends.

## Actual-model throughput

Workload:

- Model: `NVIDIA/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-NVFP4`
- MTP: three draft tokens and a four-token verification window
- Measured acceptance length: 4.0
- ReplaySSM buffer: 16
- SSM state: FP32
- Stochastic rounding: disabled
- CUDA graphs: enabled
- Metric: output tokens/s

### H100 80GB

| Batch | FlashInfer, PDL off | FlashInfer, PDL on | Triton #49847 | Best FI vs Triton |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 16 | **6,578.81** | 6,563.84 | 6,472.75 | +1.64% |
| 128 | 19,343.22 | **19,388.90** | 19,059.60 | +1.73% |
| 256 | 21,896.57 | **22,014.13** | 21,725.24 | +1.33% |
| 512 | **24,863.34** | 24,852.45 | 24,458.58 | +1.65% |

### GB200

The allocation identified the device as `NVIDIA GB200`.

| Batch | FlashInfer, PDL off | FlashInfer, PDL on | Triton #49847 | Production FI off vs Triton |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 16 | **8,811.71** | 7,921.11 | 8,467.73 | +4.06% |
| 128 | 25,532.13 | **25,948.60** | 24,270.93 | +5.20% |
| 256 | 28,687.11 | **28,703.49** | 27,153.46 | +5.65% |
| 512 | **29,272.09** | 29,170.54 | 27,718.29 | +5.61% |

PDL was harmful at GB200 B16 and effectively neutral at larger batches. The production path therefore keeps it disabled while preserving the explicit argument for future FlashInfer tuning and debugging.

## Production-profile findings

Nsight Systems profiles used 64 steady CUDA-graph decode steps and summed ReplaySSM work over all 23 Mamba layers:

| H100 case | FlashInfer kernels | Triton kernels | FlashInfer tracker | Triton tracker |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| B16, AL4 | 739.42 μs/step | 644.74 μs/step | 6.89 μs/step | 10.87 μs/step |
| B128, AL4 | 3,529.11 μs/step | 3,587.91 μs/step | 8.50 μs/step | 12.69 μs/step |

The eager microbenchmark showed a much larger FlashInfer advantage because the Triton path issued several kernels from Python. CUDA-graph replay removes most of that dispatch and inter-launch gap. In production graphs, B16 favors the Triton kernels while B128 is effectively tied; the shared FlashInfer tracker is consistently cheaper.

On GB200 at B256, ReplaySSM accounted for approximately 16% of execute-step GPU time. Its 1.56× in-model improvement predicts a maximum whole-step gain of roughly 6.1%, close to the measured 5.65%. This explains why a much larger isolated-kernel ratio becomes a mid-single-digit end-to-end improvement.

## Cache capacity

After decoupling verification length from physical state-page allocation, both backends admit the full requested concurrency:

| Batch | FlashInfer cache tokens | Triton cache tokens | Difference |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 256 | 303,923 | 308,121 | -1.4% |
| 512 | 293,990 | 299,008 | -1.7% |

This removes the previous four-state-pages-per-request over-allocation and brings FlashInfer capacity within 2% of #49847.

## Validation

- Changed-file pre-commit passes, including Ruff, mypy, SPDX, configuration validation, forbidden imports, and CUDA API checks.
- Focused H100 suite: 41 passed, 200 deselected.
- GB200 GSM8K: exact accuracy parity with zero invalid outputs.
- TP2 actual-model MTP smoke completed.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Core] Fix mamba prefill checkpoint block reservation and prompt-end eviction in align mode
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose
Enabling Mamba prefill checkpoint in the `align` mamba cache mode allows for the elimination of a second forward pass in prefill when the chunked context lengths are not multiples of the block size. In enabling prefill checkpointing for Kimi-K3 on ROCm (#58344), two issues were found where the scheduler and kv cache manager disagree on the block boundaries, causing wasted allocation and dropped cache that hurt prefix cache hits. This PR extracts the fixes to the core parts that are hardware independent out from the ROCm checkpoint enablement and addresses the following:

### 1. Surplus block reservation
The scheduler determines checkpoint positions from the prefill_end token
```
vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py's _mamba_block_aligned_split
prefill_end = max(request.num_prompt_tokens, request.num_tokens - 1)
...
checkpoint_position = get_mamba_prefill_checkpoint_position(
    prefill_end, self.hash_block_size, drop_eagle_block=self.use_eagle_block_drop,
)
...
use_internal_checkpoint = (...
    and is_mamba_prefill_checkpoint_valid(..., checkpoint_position=checkpoint_position, ...)
)
```
whereas the `MambaManager` uses a prefill chunk's end token `num_tokens`.
```
vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py's MambaManager.get_num_blocks_to_allocate()
checkpoint_position = get_mamba_prefill_checkpoint_position(
    num_tokens, self.block_pool.hash_block_size, self.drop_eagle_checkpoint_block,
)
...
# member methods that call
is_mamba_prefill_checkpoint_valid(..., checkpoint_position=checkpoint_position, ...)
...
```
As the `num_tokens`-derived `checkpoint_position` is always below the end of the prefill chunk, the `query_start < checkpoint_position < query_end` condition in `is_mamba_prefill_checkpoint_valid` is always True for MambaManager, and it allocates an additional block even for chunks that are in the middle of the requests. This makes MambaManager allocate blocks for mid-request chunks that the scheduler never plans as the scheduler only plans for blocks at the prompt-end chunks. These mid-request blocks are immediately discarded as transients, but they still consume and evict physical blocks that have held real prefix. Measured with AgentX workload at concurrency 64, these surplus block reservation can drop cache hit rate from 89% -> 49%.

This PR addresses this by using the same `prefill_end` as the scheduler to evaluate `checkpoint_position` in `MambaManager`, so that `query_start < checkpoint_position < query_end` is True only for the prompt-end chunk and checkpoint blocks are only allocated there where they're only required. This is only changed under `retention_interval == 0` where the surplus checkpoint blocks are truly redundant.

### 2. Dropped prompt-end checkpoint states (Superseded, fixed by #59146)
MambaManager's `_cache_partial_tail_block` decides whether a checkpoint block is mid-request by
```
vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py's MambaManager._cache_partial_tail_block
if (
    retention_interval == 0
    and **num_tokens < request.num_prompt_tokens**
    and checkpoint_position != request.shared_prefix_boundary
):
    self.block_pool._maybe_evict_cached_block(checkpoint_block)
    return None
```
where `num_tokens` is rounded down to block size by the HybridKVCacheCoordinator
```
def _align_cacheable(self, num_tokens: int) -> int:
    if self.enable_partial_hash_hits:
        return num_tokens
    return round_down(num_tokens, self.scheduler_block_size)

def cache_blocks(self, request, num_computed_tokens):
    cached_num_computed_tokens = self._align_cacheable(num_computed_tokens)
    ...
```

This makes last chunk of a non-multiple-of-block-size prompt rounded down to below the prompt length, and, under retention_interval=0, its hash is then removed on the same step the kernel writes it. The next conversation turn then cannot find the checkpoint states at the prompt-end boundary, and the reusable prefix becomes the last boundary or to zero, causing prefix to be recomputed.

This PR addresses this issue by adding `_is_reachable_checkpoint` where it decides if a checkpoint belongs to a prompt-end chunk using checkpoint position instead of the rounded-down count.

## Test Plan

New unit tests are added for core partial prefix cache hits:

- `test_intermediate_chunk_checkpoint_reserved_only_under_dense_retention`: prefills a prompt in two chunks and checks that the mid-prompt chunk reserves a checkpoint block only under dense retention while the prompt-end chunk reserves one either way. Fails on main under retention_interval=0.
- `test_prompt_end_checkpoint_survives_block_aligned_cache_count`: prefills a prompt whose length is not a multiple of the block size at the default match unit and checks that the prompt-end checkpoint stays in the prefix cache and that a replay of the same prompt resumes from it. Fails on main for the unaligned lengths.

## Test Result

The added unit tests pass where they fail on main branch.

The performance impact of the two issues were measured together with the ROCm Kimi-K3 mamba checkpoint enablement #58344 on MI355X. In the following benchmarks and evaluations, #58344 only adds the enablement of prefix checkpoint for Kimi-K3 on ROCm, and the pre- and post-fixes for KV cache manager and scheduler are the distinction between the main branch and this PR.

AgentX benchmark runs were performed to reflect agentic workloads with prefix caching, and different conditions were set so that the two issues could surface individually.

The issue 1 "Surplus block reservation"'s cost surfaces under memory pressure when physical blocks holding real prefix caches get evicted to make space for mid-request transient blocks that get discarded immediately. For this, the concurrency=64 AgentX benchmark setting was used.

<details>
<summary>serving command</summary>

```
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 SAFETENSORS_FAST_GPU=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_SITUV2_A8W4=1 \
       AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0 AITER_REUSE_IDENTICAL_COMM_GROUPS=1 \
```

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][PP][Spec Decode] MiniMax-M3 EAGLE3 aux-state relay at PP > 1 and per-stage FlashInfer autotune
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Enables EAGLE3 for MiniMax-M3 (NVIDIA model file) at PP > 1 on Model Runner V2, and scopes FlashInfer autotune to each PP stage's TP group, fixing a startup deadlock. Builds on #50514 (PP aux-state relay), changes the autotune sync from #50892, supersedes #57198.

Motivation: MiniMax-M3-NVFP4 PP2/TP4 + EAGLE3 serving on 8x RTX PRO 6000 (also needs #59081, which supersedes #47665). No performance claim; the speedup there comes from split-K admission (#45450 / #52879 / #56148).

## Claims

1. **MiniMax-M3 + EAGLE3 runs at PP > 1.** Base rejects it at load (`ValueError: ... does not support eagle3 with pipeline parallelism`). The drafter then gets all aux states every step; acceptance length and GSM8K match TP8.
2. **FlashInfer autotune no longer deadlocks at PP > 1** when stages tune different shapes. Each stage tunes within its TP group and writes `<cache>_tp_<ranks>.json`. PP = 1 is unchanged.

## Validation

**Setup:** 8x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120), `nvidia/MiniMax-M3-NVFP4` + `Inferact/MiniMax-M3-EAGLE3`, offline `LLM`, greedy, cold autotune. Both arms: vLLM 213c379 + FP8 Triton-indexer enablement (as in #47665; needed on SM120) + #56148's Triton-attention guard hunks (not its split-K path). Arms differ only in this PR's files as of 4683f1e3 (since then: `kernel_warmup.py` comments only; extractor hunk dropped).

| Config | Aux relay (steps) | Mean AL | GSM8K-200 spec / no-spec | Stage cache entries |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TP8 | – | 3.471 | 94.5 / 94.5 | unchanged |
| PP2/TP4 | 4600/4600 | 3.460, 3.449, 3.452 | 95.5 / 95.5 | 140 / 80 |
| PP3/TP2 | 7200/7200 | 3.469 | 94.0 / – | 140 / 80 / 80 |
| PP4/TP1 | 9200/9200 | 3.498 | 94.0 / – | 140 / 80 / 80 / 80 |

AL: 32 GSM8K prompts × 256 tokens. GSM8K-200: first 200 test questions, chat, thinking on, 0-shot, max 2048 tokens; all within ~1 SE. Autotune ≤10 s/stage.

Main engine args (PP2/TP4):
```text
-tp 4 -pp 2 --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"fp8"}'
--kv-cache-dtype fp8 --moe-backend marlin --max-model-len 65536 --language-model-only
--max-num-batched-tokens 4096 --max-num-seqs 12 --block-size 128 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95
--disable-custom-all-reduce --enable-prefix-caching --seed 0
--speculative-config '{"method":"eagle3","model":"Inferact/MiniMax-M3-EAGLE3","num_speculative_tokens":3,
  "draft_tensor_parallel_size":4,"attention_backend":"TRITON_ATTN","use_local_argmax_reduction":true}'
```

**Base** (same image, base files):
- With these args: the `ValueError` on all 8 ranks.
- Without `--speculative-config`: hangs in autotune; `--kernel-config '{"enable_flashinfer_autotune": false}'` avoids it. PR `model.py` with base `kernel_warmup.py` + EAGLE3 hangs too (both changes needed).
- Non-spec PP2/TP4 (autotune off, 16 prompts, two setups): identical greedy outputs 2–3/16 PR vs base, 2–5/16 PR vs PR (mean hidden cosine .95–.97): no detectable PR effect.

**Non-MiniMax, H200:** Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 bf16 PP2/TP2, PR vs base: both start; PR writes per-stage caches; GSM8K-200 96.0 vs 95.5 (default MoE, 0 tuned entries), 95.5 vs 94.0 (`flashinfer_cutlass`, 44 entries/stage): equivalent.

**Pre-existing, not fixed here:** a warm restart with a `flashinfer_cutlass` cache at PP2/TP2 hangs in base and PR (TP rank 0 hits the cache, rank 1 re-tunes); matches #57423 (fixes: #57579, #57635; untested).

@SloptimistPrime reported the autotune fix on 6x GB10 (SM121), TP2/PP3 (#57198); their test commit 1291f3fe is not included.

**CPU tests and lint:**
```bash
pytest -q tests/model_executor/test_flashinfer_autotune_warmup.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_eagle3_aux_hidden_states_pp.py
# 17 passed (11 added). Production files reverted: 8 of the 11 fail
# (incl. PP = 1 layer-0 tap); the 3 passing are PP = 1 / no-aux guards.
pre-commit run --hook-stage manual --files $(git diff --name-only 5c3b61e9)
# all pass, incl. mypy 3.10-3.13 and test tethering
```

## Details

**Root cause, autotune.** Since #50892 all ranks sync over the world group (cache broadcast, barrier, per-tactic all-reduce). PP stages can tune different shapes (140 vs 80 `mxfp8_gemm` entries), so PP0 waits on a collective PP1 never joins. Fix: at PP > 1, leader, broadcast, barrier, timing average and cache file use the stage's TP group.

**Root cause, MiniMax-M3.** No #50514 opt-in; taps used stage-local layer indices. Fix: set `supports_aux_hidden_states_over_pp` and use the `EagleModelMixin` helpers (global indices, pack local / collect upstream taps), like Llama, Qwen2, DeepSeek-V4, Kimi-K3. Tap 0 aliases `residual`, which fused add-RMSNorm updates in place, so it is cloned when layer 0 is a tap (any PP size; CPU-tested; GPU runs above use taps 2/30/57).

**Dropped:** #57290's `extract_hidden_states` draft PP = 1 hunk (extractor-only; EAGLE3 unaffected): at PP2 it turned a config-time `NotImplementedError` into a startup `AssertionError` (`ExampleHiddenStatesConnector` needs a change; separate PR). Supersedes earlier status comments.

**Size and tradeoffs.** 2 production files, +40/−13. Tests +342/−2 (CPU fakes). At PP > 1, old unsuffixed caches are not read (one re-tune) and stages may pick different tactics for the same shape (unmeasured). Each PP hop carries one extra `[tokens, hidden]` tensor per upstream tap (not benchmarked).

**Limits.** Aux relay is V2-only (V1: #45985); the autotune change also affects V1 (not run). Untested: MiniMax-M3 dflash/dspark and multimodal inputs at PP > 1 (both now accepted), ROCm (AMD model file unchanged), DP > 1 with PP > 1, MiniMax-M3 FlashInfer MoE (runs used Marlin). CI gap: `test_eagle3_aux_hidden_states_pp.py` does not run on `vllm/models/`-only changes. #57579, #57635, #55671, #52292 also edit `flashinfer_autotune` (on conflict, keep the per-stage group); #53901 reworks the PP aux helpers. No duplicate found.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Stop the host pool feeding device KV cache residency metrics
commits.pr_body:
> **NOTE:** This PR was reduced to a one-line change: the HiSparse host pool no longer gets the device pool's metrics collector (`metrics_collector=None` in `HiSparseSourceManager.bind_host_pool`), so host blocks stop feeding the device `vllm:kv_block_*_seconds` histograms. That removes the block-ID collision described below at its source, instead of keying samples by pool. Host-tier residency metrics are proposed separately in #59485 (on top of #58949). The description below is the original.

## Purpose

With HiSparse and `--kv-cache-metrics`, the host and GPU pools share a metrics
collector, but each pool numbers its blocks independently. The collector keys
samples by `block_id` alone.

This results in incorrect metrics recording in KV cache block activities
when using HiSparse.

A false lifetime, idle-time, and reuse-gap histogram will affect users
relying on it to investigate cache turnover and reuse.

For example, allocate GPU block 1 at t=1 s and host block 1 at t=2 s. The host
allocation currently emits a false one-second GPU eviction sample, even though
the GPU block remains allocated. With this fix, **both histories remain active
and no eviction sample is emitted**.

This MR key samples by `(block.pool, block.block_id)` in allocation, access
and eviction callbacks. Allowing the KV cache block activities to be correctly
accounted.


The callbacks only update telemetry; allocation and eviction decisions are
unaffected. Ordinary hybrid/SWA groups sharing one pool retain their existing
behavior.


## Test Coverage

`test_hisparse_host_pool_preserves_device_lifecycle`
(`tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_connector.py:59`) verifies the
production-wiring example. The test fails with metrics enabled without the fix.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Adopt GPU prefix copies after the hit's allocation
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fix an engine crash (`Cannot get N free blocks from the pool`) on a HiSparse host-prefix hit under GPU memory pressure. This is an alternative to #57457.

Closes #59440.

"Adopting" a GPU copy means a host-prefix hit points its page at a still-valid GPU copy of that host page (a GPU-side prefix-cache hit) instead of reading the page back from host.

A host-prefix hit re-pins free GPU copies of its pages so the prefix comes back GPU-resident. Admission counts those copies as free blocks, but adoption pinned them before the hit's own allocation (hot region and new pages), which could then run the pool dry.

#57457 fixes this by charging the pins at admission. That mixes host and GPU accounting in `HiSparseSourceManager.get_num_blocks_to_allocate`, and under pressure it defers a request that could run by reading its prefix from host, just to keep an optimization.

## Changes

HiSparse-only (`vllm/v1/hisparse/coordinator.py`):

- **Adopt after allocation.** `commit_computed_blocks` records the pages to adopt, and `update_residency` (in `cache_blocks`, after `allocate_new_blocks`) adopts the copies that survived. The allocation always gets what admission counted, so no admission accounting is needed. A copy the allocation reuses is dropped by its reuse watcher and never adopted.
- **Tail first.** HiSparse releases a prefix's pages tail first, matching `free_blocks`' convention, so pressure trims a prefix from its end.

Replaying #57457's scenario (a resumed 3-page host prefix hit, `free_blocks` left in the pool):

| `free_blocks` | main | #57457 | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5–6 | rejected | rejected | rejected |
| 7–8 | crash | rejected | admitted, 0/3 copies |
| 9 | crash | rejected | admitted, 1/3 |
| 10 | 3/3 | 3/3 | 2/3 |
| 11+ | 3/3 | 3/3 | 3/3 |

Near the boundary this keeps fewer copies than #57457, because blocks freed after the copies are queued behind them. #59283, stacked on this PR, is an optional core change that restores 3/3 at 10.

## Test Plan

- `test_hisparse_prefix_hit_under_pressure_adopts_surviving_copies[7, 10]`: exact adopted pages, and no block shared between adopted copies and fresh allocations. `7` fails without the adoption timing, and `10` without tail-first release.
- `tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py` and `tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py`, with `CpuPlatform` selected:

```bash
python cpu_pytest.py --confcutdir=tests/v1/core tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py
```

## Test Result

- Both new cases fail on main and pass with this PR.
- CPU (`CpuPlatform`): 295 passed. 8 errors are `fixture 'caplog_vllm' not found`, from running outside the top-level conftest, and are identical on main.
- H100, HiSparse unit tests across `tests/v1` (`-k hisparse`): 156 passed.
- H100, `test_prefix_caching.py` + `test_kv_cache_utils.py`: 301 passed. The 2 failures (`test_get_kv_cache_config_mamba_hybrid_sharing_pp_*`) need 4 visible GPUs and fail identically on main with 1.
- H100, `tests/v1/e2e/general/test_hisparse.py`: fails with this PR alone (see the dependency note); with #59235 merged in, 2 passed in each of 2 runs.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][MiniMax-M3] Triton indexer: decode grid retune + SM12.0 split-K
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Two changes to the Triton MiniMax-M3 indexer (`vllm/models/minimax_m3/common/ops/index_topk.py`):

1. **Decode launch-grid retune.** `TARGET_GRID` goes from 512 to 4096 (decode index score) and `TOPK_TARGET_GRID` from 64 to 512 (decode top-k). This applies to every CUDA GPU on the Triton MiniMax-M3 indexer, not only SM120. ROCm uses its own `amd/ops/index_topk.py` and is not touched. Folded in from #49229 with its author's agreement; original commit by Zijing Liu, co-authored by Kyle Liang.
2. **SM12.0 prefill split-K.** On SM12.0 only, the prefill index score (`_index_block_score_kernel`) splits its K loop across CTAs when the launch grid is small, as it is for short chunked-prefill extends. Other GPUs keep the unsplit launch.

This PR was closed after the concurrency-12 point showed no gain, then reopened and narrowed:
- FP8 index-cache support and the operand casts are in #59081 (supersedes #47665).
- The fused decode top-k and the router change are dropped.

## Claims

Faster decode at higher batch sizes on the Triton indexer (grid retune), and faster short-extend prefill on RTX PRO 6000 (SM120, split-K).

## Validation

- **E2E:** MiniMax-M3-NVFP4 + EAGLE3 on 8x RTX PRO 6000, InferenceMAX recipe at c10 TP8.
  - Grid retune: removing it costs 4.6% throughput (tput 0.954x). Decode step p50 at 10 requests is 49.2 ms without it and 39.6 ms with it, matching the reference stack's 39.6 ms. #49229 separately reported +44% at B300 TP4 c24.
  - Split-K: short cached extends take 263 ms per iteration without it and 200 ms with it (reference stack 192 ms). This comes from a leave-one-out of the earlier fused-top-k + split-K version; split-K is the only part of that version on this path.
  - This PR as a whole: the split-K-only confirmation run already included the grid retune, so it measures exactly these contents. It reaches 0.985 tput / 1.004 interactivity vs the InferenceMAX reference stack, and per-request TPOT 0.997 [0.975, 1.008] vs the earlier fused+split-K version (n=1).
- **SM120 tests:** `pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3.py` gives 95 passed, 0 failed, 58 skipped. Main gives 92 / 0 / 58; the only difference is the 3 new prefill cases, and outcomes on the shared IDs are identical. `test_decode_index_topk_correctness` passes all 6 cases with the new decode grids (256 score chunks; up to 16 top-k chunks). All 4 prefill cases take `USE_SPLIT_K=True`.
- **CI:** `test_prefill_index_topk_correctness` forces the split path on any CUDA GPU (incl. an uneven split), so L4 runs it.
- **Lint:** `pre-commit`, including mypy-3.12, passed.

## Details

- Decode chunk counts stay shape-constant, so the launch is still CUDA-graph safe. At 2 or fewer decode requests the score grid is unchanged, because both values hit the 256-chunk cap.
- The split count is `split_k = min(max_block, 48 // (n_q_tiles * batch * heads))`, on SM12.0 only.
- Each CTA writes a disjoint range of per-block maxima, so no reduction is needed.
- Splits past a query tile's causal window exit early.
